title: Binary versus Continuous Dose Designs for Two-Response Activity Screening under Shared Noise Scale
banked_reason: D0.5 tier=incremental < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 5.6 < 7.4. Math panel passed with five citations verified; unrepaired negative_target_missing and ballast_duplicate preserved in receipts.
gap_reasons: The delivered contribution is a sharp asymptotic design characterization for one two-factor, two-response prior-predictive benchmark, which earns subfield rather than field significance. The stitched proofs supply the moving-matrix converse and separate optimizer scales; the remaining open localization questions do not leave those headline results deferred, and the framing does not advertise their completion. The new power advantage occurs only below ν=√2−1, whereas the motivating [DABS calibration](https://arxiv.org/html/2607.16927v1#S3) uses inverse-gamma shape three, corresponding to ν=6, where Hadamard menus attain the first frontier. The operational comparison therefore establishes an eventual entropy-deficit gain under prospective heavy-tail calibrations without establishing its magnitude or onset at usable finite signals. The finite certificate proves termination but supplies neither an implementation nor certified evaluations, leaving the paper's practical design significance insufficiently demonstrated for a leading econometrics journal. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.6 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]

No Lean formalization was attempted; finite-signal implementation and certified gains remain future work, and the negative-target and duplicate-wrapper panel cautions remain unrepaired.
